title: A Survey on Retrieval-Augmented Generation: From Naive to Modular RAG
tldr: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), categorizing its development into Naive, Advanced, and Modular paradigms.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) face significant challenges including hallucinations, outdated knowledge, and non-transparent reasoning, particularly in knowledge-intensive tasks. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses these issues by integrating external knowledge from dynamic repositories into the LLM inference process. This paper categorizes the evolution of RAG into three main paradigms: Naive RAG, Advanced RAG, and Modular RAG, while analyzing key technologies in retrieval, generation, and augmentation. The survey also introduces an up-to-date evaluation framework and summarizes current assessment methods covering 26 tasks and nearly 50 datasets.
problem_statement: LLMs suffer from hallucinations when handling queries beyond their training data and struggle with outdated or domain-specific information. Prior methods like unsupervised fine-tuning often fail to help LLMs learn new factual information effectively, creating a need for a system that can bridge the information gap using external databases.
key_contributions: Categorized the RAG research landscape into three distinct paradigms: Naive RAG, Advanced RAG, and Modular RAG.
Provided a detailed technical analysis of the tripartite RAG foundation: Retrieval, Generation, and Augmentation.
Summarized current assessment methods, covering 26 tasks and nearly 50 datasets, and introduced an up-to-date evaluation framework.
Analyzed the evolution of RAG from inference-only stages to integrated fine-tuning and pre-training techniques.

architecture.overview: The RAG framework is built on a tripartite foundation consisting of retrieval, generation, and augmentation, evolving from a simple sequential pipeline to complex modular systems.
components: Retrieval: Locates relevant document chunks using semantic similarity.
Generation: Synthesizes the query and retrieved context into a coherent response.
Augmentation: Integrates retrieved information into the prompt or model process.
key_design_choices: Naive RAG uses a 'Retrieve-Read' framework for simplicity.
Advanced RAG introduces pre-retrieval and post-retrieval optimization to improve quality.
Modular RAG allows for non-sequential processing and module substitution for greater flexibility.

methods: Indexing: Splitting documents into chunks, encoding them into vectors, and storing them in a vector databases.
Retrieval: Computing similarity scores between query vectors and stored chunk vectors to find Top-k results.
Query Optimization: Using methods like query rewriting, transformation, and expansion to improve retrieval.
Post-retrieval: Employing re-ranking and context compression to refine the information sent to the LLM.
Modular components: Utilizing specialized modules like Search (for engines/KGs), Memory (to guide retrieval), and TaskAdapter (for downstream tasks).

other: RAG research stages include pre-training, fine-tuning, and inference.

results: RAG consistently outperforms unsupervised fine-tuning for both existing knowledge and entirely new knowledge in knowledge-intensive tasks.
Advanced and Modular RAG are noted to be cost-effective and surpass the performance of native LLMs.
baselines_compared: Unsupervised Fine-Tuning — RAG outperforms this for learning new factual information.
Prompt Engineering — Differentiated by lower requirements for external knowledge and model adaptation.
Naive RAG — Used as a baseline for Advanced and Modular paradigms.
ablation_findings: The paper notes that feeding all relevant documents directly into LLMs can lead to information overload and dilute focus on key details.
datasets: Wikipedia — Primary retrieval source for many ODQA tasks.
CommonCrawl — Used in pre-training iterative RAG models like Atlas.
MSMARCO — Used for tuning in AAR.
HotpotQA — A version of the dataset dated 1st October, 2017.
limitations: Retrieval challenges: Issues with precision, recall, selection of misaligned/irrelevant chunks, and missing crucial information.
Generation challenges: Hallucinations (content not supported by context), irrelevance, toxicity, or bias.
Augmentation challenges: Redundancy from multiple sources, difficulty mining significance, and maintaining stylistic/tonal consistency.
Semi-structured data: Conventional text splitting can corrupt tables in PDFs, complicating semantic searches.
future_work: Integrating RAG with other technologies like reinforcement learning.
Improving the handling of semi-structured and structured data (Knowledge Graphs).
Refining the interaction between RAG and fine-tuning to achieve optimal results.
related_work_context: RAG research emerged alongside the Transformer architecture and has evolved from early pre-training model (PTM) refinements to the paradigm shift caused by ChatGPT's in-context learning capabilities.
impact_and_significance: This work provides a roadmap for the field, moving from simple retrieval-read pipelines to highly flexible modular architectures that enable real-time knowledge updates and high interpretability in LLMs.
